title.narrative: Integrated Response to Gender-Based Violence in Conflict-Affected Woredas of North Gojjam and South Gonder Zones, Amhara Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project titled “Integrated Response to Gender-Based Violence in Conflict-Affected Woredas of North Gojjam Zone, Amhara Region” is designed to respond to the urgent and widespread protection needs of women and girls caused by ongoing conflict and displacement. A needs assessment conducted in May 2025 revealed extremely high rates of gender-based violence (GBV), including rape, intimate partner violence, and sexual exploitation. These incidents have been exacerbated by the breakdown of local protection systems and the near-total absence of GBV case management services, trained personnel, Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS), and one-stop centers. There is also a critical shortage of emergency cash assistance, dignity kits, and community awareness on GBV, child protection, and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), resulting in stigma, fear, and underreporting.ltbrgtThe overarching goal of the project is to reduce GBV risks and improve access to comprehensive, survivor-centered response services for conflict-affected women and girls. The project specifically aims to restore GBV case management and referral pathways, expand access to Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), provide life-saving multi-purpose cash assistance, and raise community awareness to shift social norms that tolerate or normalize GBV. To achieve this, the project will implement a set of integrated and context-specific strategies. These include training caseworkers and community health professionals in survivor-centered approaches and trauma-informed care delivering Psychological First Aid (PFA) constructing and equipping four Women and Girls Safe Spaces and strengthening the GBV response capacity of health centers and Women and Social Affairs offices. Additionally, the project will distribute dignity kits to address the hygiene and protection needs of women and girls and will offer emergency cash assistance to 1,000 GBV survivors to help remove economic barriers to accessing safety and essential services.ltbrgtCommunity engagement is a central component of the project. Through community-led dialogues and targeted sensitization campaigns, the project will raise awareness about GBV and available services, promote reporting, and challenge harmful gender norms. The project is scheduled to run for 12 months, from July 15, 2025, to July 14, 2026, in six conflict-affected woredas: Semen Achefer, Debub Mecha, Mecha, Gonje, Ebnat, and Menametewa. It targets internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities, with a strong focus on the inclusion of older women and persons with disabilities, who often face heightened vulnerability in humanitarian settings.ltbrgtBased on the needs assessment, the project aims to reach a total of 39,847 people, disaggregated as follows: 21,916 women (aged 18 and above), 9,961 girls (under 18), 5,180 men (aged 18 and above), and 2,790 boys (under 18). This includes 15,540 individuals from internally displaced populations, 4,782 returnees, and 15,540 people from host communities. The approach is inclusive and intersectional, ensuring that no group is left behind in the response.ltbrgtWith a total budget of $649,999.97, the initiative will contribute meaningfully to national protection cluster objectives and humanitarian priorities. It will deliver immediate, life-saving support for survivors while building local systems and community capacities for long-term GBV prevention and response. By strengthening institutional response mechanisms, empowering frontline workers, and mobilizing community support, the project will lay the groundwork for a more protective and equitable environment for women and girls across the six woredas of North Gojjam Zone.ltbrgtlt/pgt
